FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: mapo doufu
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: cubes of {0_adj} tofu slipped into a red sauce of fermented beans, with minced {2_coll} and Sichuan pepper that numbs the tongue before {1_coll} burns it.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: char siu
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: strips of {0_adj} lacquered with honey and {2_plur}, hung on hooks over the fire until the edges blacken. The name means cooked on a fork.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: xiaolongbao
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: dumplings pleated eighteen times, filled with {1_plur} and a jelly of stock that turns back to liquid in the steam. You pierce them before biting, on pain of a burn.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: gong bao
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} in dice fried so fast that the wok never cools, with whole {2_coll} left in the oil and {1_coll} added last of all so as to stay crisp.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: hongshao rou
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: cubes of {0_adj} caramelised in {1_coll} melted dry before they are stewed with {2_plur}. The sugar has to brown without bitterness: a few seconds part the two.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: dan dan noodles
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: noodles served over a pool of {1_adj} paste and {2_adj} oil, to be mixed by the eater. The name comes from the carrying pole of the hawkers who bore them.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: wonton
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: squares of dough so fine that the {1_adj} filling shows through, closed with a pinch and poached in a {2_adj} broth. The tail of dough floats and ripples: that is what gave them their name.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: peking duck
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a bird blown full of air to lift the skin off the flesh, scalded, lacquered with {1_plur} and dried a day in the wind before roasting. The skin is served first, in fine pancakes, and the meat afterwards.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: cantonese fried rice
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: yesterday's {0_coll}, dry and loose grain by grain, fried at the highest flame with {1_plur} and {2_plur}. Fresh rice clumps and turns to porridge: it has to have slept.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: chicken with cashews
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} coated in starch and blanched in warm oil before it meets the wok — that is what keeps it tender — then fried with {2_plur} and toasted {1_coll}.
